text: Draw one card, plus more cards based on your Peaceful enclaves on the map: +1 if you have 2–3, +2 if you have 4–7, or +3 if you have 8 or more. Then, if you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.

title: Overview
text: The Twilight Council works to suppress violence by bringing together the Woodfolk in ASSEMBLIES, hoping to draw the civil war to an end. Assemblies let the Council score victory points, banish enemy warriors from their clearings, and gain LOYALISTS, warriors on their player board that they can later place at assemblies. The Council acts as PEACEKEEPERS at their assemblies, defending enemy factions when they're attacked. By ruling assemblies, the Council can flip assemblies to their GOVERNING side. In Evening, they score points based on the number of Governing assemblies with any enemy buildings or tokens at them. Their GOVERNORS limit the actions that enemies can take at Governing assemblies, unless those enemies ENTREAT the Council to close the assembly for a time.

title: Loyalists
text: The Council can hold up to 4 warriors on its player board as LOYALISTS. They can place Loyalists with Entreat (17.2.4) and Assemble (17.4.3). They may remove Loyalists at any time.

title: Assemblies
text: Assemblies have two sides: Closed (closed tent) and Governing (open tent). When an enemy of the Council removes an assembly, the Council removes 1 Loyalist.

title: Governors
text: At Governing assemblies, enemies of the Council cannot activate crafting pieces and cannot place, take, remove, or flip pieces, except in battle. (The Vagabond cannot craft because the Vagabond pawn is its crafting piece.)

title: Entreat
text: Any number of times on their turn, an enemy may force the Council to flip any assembly to Closed. After flipping it, the Council may either place any number of Loyalists at that assembly or place 1 warrior in their Loyalists.

title: Peacekeepers
text: When an enemy chooses another enemy as defender at an assembly, the Council adds Council warriors as defending warriors, but Council warriors only take hits once the defender's warriors have been removed. Ignore Peacekeepers if the Vagabond is defending. (The Council cannot ambush, use battle effects, etc.)

title: Vagabond Allies
text: If the Vagabond attacks another enemy in battle while Allied (9.2.9.II) to the Twilight Council, Council warriors are attacking warriors.

title: Crafting
text: The Council crafts during Evening by activating assemblies.

title: Step 1: Gather Pieces
text: Form a supply of 20 warriors.

title: Step 2: Place Warriors
text: Place 4 warriors in a corner clearing. This is your starting clearing. Place 2 warriors in a different clearing.

title: Step 3: Fill Assemblies Track
text: Fill your Assemblies track on your player board with your 6 assemblies.

title: Birdsong
text: Any number of times, you may reveal a card to take an action, as follows. (Reveal cards from your hand into your play area. They cannot be used for any other purposes during Birdsong.)

title: Move
text: Take a move from a clearing matching the revealed card.

title: Recruit
text: Place 1 warrior in a clearing matching the revealed card.

title: Assemble
text: Place a Closed assembly and any number of Loyalists in a clearing matching the revealed card that has no assembly. Then, if you don't rule the clearing, discard the revealed card.

title: Battle
text: Initiate a battle in a clearing matching the revealed card. If an assembly is there, discard the revealed card.

title: Sleep
text: Flip assemblies ruled by enemies to Closed.

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has five steps in the following order.

title: Convene Woodfolk
text: One by one, return each card that you revealed in Birdsong to your hand. For each card returned, you may take one of the following actions.

title: Banish
text: If you returned a non-bird card, initiate a battle in a clearing with a matching assembly. Defending warriors are not removed when hit; instead, force them to move to a single destination you choose, ignoring rule. Treat this as a single move for triggering other effects. You cannot hit buildings or tokens, and you ignore rolled hits you take (not ambush or extra hits).

title: The Warlord
text: The warlord cannot take hits from banish because it cannot be moved outside the Lord of the Hundred's turn. (Their other warriors still take hits.)

title: The Vagabond
text: The Vagabond cannot take hits from banish because it is not a warrior.

title: Hirelings
text: Hirelings cannot take hits from banish because they cannot be forced to move (H.3.4).

title: Agitate
text: If you returned a non-bird card, spend it and choose a matching assembly. Place 1 warrior in your Loyalists, then flip the assembly to Governing if it is Closed. (You cannot gain the Loyalist if you don't have a matching assembly.)

title: Empower
text: If you returned a bird card, choose an assembly. Roll one battle die and remove Council warriors from it equal to the rolled number. You may either place these warriors in your Loyalists, or you may score 1 victory point if you rule the assembly.

title: Inspire
text: You may activate assemblies to craft cards. If you craft no cards, draw one card per card draw icon showing on your Assemblies track.

title: Adjourn
text: You may remove any of your assemblies. Flip assemblies you rule to Governing.

title: Oversee
text: Score victory points based on the number of Governing assemblies in the same clearing as any enemy buildings or tokens. For one assembly, score one point; for two or three, score two points; for four, score three points; for five or six, score four points.

title: Draw and Discard
text: Draw one card. Then, if you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.

title: Overview
text: The Knaves of the Deepwood endeavor to mock the powerful and protect the needy. Each turn, they score victory points from their ACCLAIM throughout the Woodland and from warriors they take as PRISONERS by battling the enemy factions. Each turn, they act with one of their three CAPTAINS, backed up by a crew of rowdy SKUNKS that can move along with them. However, once a Captain has acted, it cannot act again until after the Knaves act with all three Captains, letting them TAKE IT EASY. They have a STASH of items that they can flip face down to take special actions at their Captain. Like their Captains, their items only flip face up again once they Take It Easy.

title: Exclusive with Vagabond
text: The Knaves of the Deepwood cannot be played in the same game as the Vagabond.

title: Stash
text: Instead of a Crafted Items box, the Knaves have the STASH. It holds items, which can be face up or face down. When you craft or take an item, place it face up in your Stash.

title: Acclaim
text: The Knaves have 8 acclaim tokens. Each clearing can hold one acclaim. (Forests cannot hold it.) Acclaim affects various actions (18.5.1) and scores victory points in Evening (18.6.1).

title: Deepwood Runners
text: Captains and Skunks are warriors that can move in and out of forests, ignoring rule.

title: Follow Me
text: When moving a Captain, the Knaves may move Skunks with the Captain. Captains can only be hit in battle if no Skunks remain in the battle clearing. Captains cannot be placed except in setup and with Ready (18.4), and cannot be replaced.

title: Have at Thee
text: When an Acting Captain attacks a faction in battle, the Knaves take 1 defending warrior they hit as a prisoner: instead of removing it, they move it to an adjacent forest with no Prisoners, ignoring rule. If it cannot be moved, remove it as normal. At the end of this battle, place acclaim in the battle clearing if the Acting Captain is there.

title: Run Away
text: When an enemy removes acclaim, they force the Knaves to place 1 Skunk in a forest of the enemy's choice adjacent to the acclaim's former clearing. (If the Skunk supply is empty, ignore this.)

title: Crafting
text: The Knaves craft in Daylight by activating their Acting Captain or acclaim. Their Filch (18.5.1.III) lets them activate their Acting Captain, and their Serve (18.5.1.IVg) lets them activate any number of acclaim matching their Acting Captain's clearing. Each acclaim can only be activated once per turn.

title: Step 1: Gather Pieces
text: Form a supply of 10 Skunk warriors.

title: Step 2: Choose Captains
text: Choose 3 Captain cards. Collect their respective Captain warriors.

title: Step 3: Place Captains and Skunks
text: Place 1 Captain warrior and 1 Skunk warrior each in three different forests.

title: Step 4: Set Up Player Board
text: Place the 6 items face up in your Stash that are shown on your 3 chosen Captain cards. Fill each Acclaim slot with 2 acclaim tokens.

title: Birdsong
text: READY. Place a face-up Captain card in the Acting Captain slot on your player board. You gain the effect listed on this card until you Retire (18.5.2). If the corresponding Captain warrior is not on the map, place it in any forest, remove any Prisoners in that forest and adjacent forests, and you take only three actions during Captain Acts (18.5.1).

title: Daylight
text: Your Daylight has two steps in the following order.

title: Captain Acts
text: In any order and combination, you may take up to four actions as follows with the Acting Captain, shown in your Acting Captain slot. (If the Acting Captain was placed in a forest with Ready in Birdsong this turn, you take up to three actions instead.)

title: Move
text: Take a move with the Acting Captain. (You may move Skunks along with it.)

title: Battle
text: Initiate a battle in the Acting Captain's clearing.

title: Filch
text: Once per turn, either craft a card by activating the Acting Captain, or take 1 item from the Crafted Items box of an enemy faction in the Acting Captain's clearing. If you craft an item with Filch, do not score its listed victory points.

title: Item Action
text: Flip a face-up item in your Stash face down to take its action.

title: Dash ()
text: {boot}}). Move the Acting Captain up to twice, ignoring rule.

title: Assault ()
text: {sword}}). Initiate a battle in the Acting Captain's clearing. Take all warriors you hit as a Prisoner (18.2.6), moving each to a separate forest with no Prisoners.

title: Skirmish ()
text: {crossbow}}). Move the Acting Captain from a forest. Then, initiate a battle in the Acting Captain's destination clearing, ignoring the first hit you take.

title: Nab ()
text: {sack}}). Initiate a battle in the Acting Captain's clearing. If the Acting Captain is hit, it is not removed—move it to an adjacent forest instead; if it cannot be moved, it is removed as normal. If the Acting Captain was not hit, you may move it after the battle (after placing acclaim).

title: Revel ()
text: {tea}}). Place 1 acclaim and 1 Skunk at the Acting Captain. (If it's in a forest, just place the Skunk.) If acclaim is already in the Acting Captain's clearing, place 2 Skunks there instead.

title: Gift ()
text: {coin}}). Place 1 acclaim in the Acting Captain's clearing and draw 1 card. (If it's in a forest, just draw 1 card.) If acclaim is already in the Acting Captain's clearing, draw 2 cards instead.

title: Serve ()
text: {hammer}}). Place 1 acclaim in the Acting Captain's clearing. If acclaim is already in the Acting Captain's clearing, activate any number of acclaim matching the Acting Captain's clearing to craft cards instead. (You do score the listed points. Each acclaim can only be activated once per turn to craft.)

title: Retire
text: Flip the Captain card in the Acting Captain slot face down and return it to your supply.

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has four steps in the following order.

title: Mock the Powerful
text: Score 1 victory point for every 2 Prisoners, and score 1 victory point for every 2 acclaim on the map.

title: Protect the Weak
text: Once per acclaim, you may spend a matching card to place 1 Skunk at it.

title: Take It Easy
text: If all three Captain cards are face down, flip them face up, flip all items in your Stash face up, and the enemy with the most Prisoners may choose a clearing, remove all Prisoners of their faction from adjacent forests, and place them into the chosen clearing. On a tie for most Prisoners, you choose one tied enemy.

title: Draw and Discard
text: Draw one card. Then, if you have more than five cards in your hand, discard cards of your choice until you have five.

title: Step 1: Choose And Set Up Map
text: As a group, choose a map. If you choose a variant map (M), follow its Setup Modification section, then collect the 12 suit markers, flip them face down, and shuffle them, then place one on each clearing, covering the printed suit symbols if any. Set up the ruins (5.1.4), item supply (5.1.5), and dice (5.1.6) as normal.

title: Step 2: Choose Deck
text: As a group, you may choose to replace the entire shared deck from the base game with the Exiles and Partisans deck or Squires and Disciples deck.

title: Step 3: Set Up Bots
text: As a group, you may choose to play with bots, as described in the Law of Rootbotics.

title: Step 4: Seat Players
text: Determine the seating order and the first player randomly.

title: Step 5: Set Up Landmarks
text: As a group, you may choose to use landmarks (L). If so, you may ignore or override the placement of the Tower and Ferry pieces in Maps (M).

title: Step 1: Choose
text: As a group, choose if you're playing with one or two landmarks, and remove any landmark cards you do not want to play with.

title: Step 2: Deal and Collect
text: Shuffle the chosen landmark cards, deal out the chosen number, and collect the landmark piece shown on each dealt card.

title: Step 3: Set Up
text: The last player in turn order sets up one drawn landmark as described on its card. If you chose to play with two landmarks, the second-to-last player in turn order sets up the other drawn landmark as described on its card.

title: Step 6: Set Up Hirelings
text: As a group, you may choose to use exactly three hirelings (H), as follows.

title: Step 1: Collect Pieces
text: Shuffle all the hirelings cards. Deal out three hireling cards and return the rest to the box. Collect the pieces for the dealt hireling cards into a supply.

title: Step 2: Demote
text: If playing with three players, flip over one random hireling to its Demoted side (marked with a "D"). If playing with four players, flip over two random hirelings to their Demoted side. If playing with five or more players, flip over all three hirelings to their Demoted side.

title: Step 3: Set Up Hirelings
text: Starting with the last player in turn order and going counterclockwise, players set up one dealt hireling each as described on its hireling card. (Some have no setup instructions.)

title: Step 4: Place Hireling Markers
text: Place the three hireling markers—marked "4," "8," and "12"—on the "4," "8," and "12" spaces of the score track on the map.

title: Step 5: Return Corresponding Factions
text: A faction cannot be played if its corresponding hireling is in play, shown by its color and icon. (The Exile/Brigand hireling removes both the Vagabond and Knaves of the Deepwood.) Return the corresponding faction boards, pieces, and setup cards to the box.

title: Step 7: Draw Five Cards
text: If you are playing with two players, remove all four dominance cards from the deck. Shuffle the deck. Each player draws five cards. (Not three, as in Standard Setup! You will choose three cards to keep in step 10.)

title: Step 8: Set Up Factions
text: As a group, you may choose and set up factions as described in the Standard Setup (5.1) or you may use the faction setup cards included in the Marauder and Homeland Expansions, as described below.

title: Step 1: Create Draft Pool
text: Agree whether you will omit any factions from the game. You cannot include both the Vagabond and the Knaves of the Deepwood. If you include the Vagabond, choose whether to include one or both Vagabond setup cards. (We recommend one card except for adventurous groups.)

title: Step 2: Deal Setup Cards
text: Shuffle all of the militant faction setup cards (red name with sword) and deal out one card to a pool in the center of the table. Shuffle the remaining militant faction setup cards together with all of the insurgent faction setup cards (grey name with no sword), and deal out one faction setup card per player. (There will be one more faction setup card than the number of players.)

title: Two Players
text: If you're playing with two players, remove all of the insurgent faction setup cards before dealing out any. (You may keep them if you're playing with hirelings and feeling adventurous.)

title: Lock Last Insurgent
text: If the last faction setup card dealt out is an insurgent, turn it sideways to show that it is locked. It cannot be chosen unless at least one militant faction has been chosen.

title: Vagabond
text: Whenever a Vagabond faction setup card is dealt out, also deal out one random character card next to it face up. If a player chooses this Vagabond as their faction, they must use this character card.

title: Knaves
text: Whenever the Knaves of the Deepwood faction setup card is dealt out, also deal out four random Captain cards next to it face up. (In their setup, they will choose three.)

title: Step 3: Choose Factions
text: Starting with the last player in turn order and going counterclockwise, each player chooses one faction setup card from the pool and sets up the faction immediately as it describes (before another player chooses).

title: Homelands
text: When setting up, players might choose one or more homeland clearings. Players cannot choose homelands that enemies have chosen as their homelands or where they cannot place all the pieces listed in setup.

title: Enemy Homeland Adjacency
text: Some factions require you to choose a homeland that is not adjacent to enemy homelands; if you cannot do this, choose a homeland adjacent to an enemy homeland. If you must choose a homeland that has two or more clearings between it and enemy homelands but you cannot, choose a homeland that is not adjacent to enemy homelands. (Basically, try to set up as far away as able.)

title: Multiple Homeland Adjacency
text: If your faction has multiple homelands and you cannot fulfill all of their enemy adjacency requirements (A.8.3.II), choose and set them up one at a time, fulfilling each requirement as best you can.

title: Step 9: Place Score Markers
text: Each player places their faction's score marker on the "0" space on the score track.

title: Step 10: Choose Starting Hands
text: Each player chooses three cards in their hand to keep and puts the other two cards face down on the shared deck. When finished, shuffle the shared deck.

title: Ability
text: A persistent effect of a faction as listed at the top of its faction board and in its Faction Rules and Abilities section, or a persistent effect of a hireling as listed on its hireling card (H.2.2).

title: Adjacent
text: A clearing is adjacent to all other clearings linked to it by a path. A forest is adjacent to all clearings that touch it without crossing a path, and it is adjacent to all forests that are separated by only one path, except on the lake (M.3.4).

title: Building
text: A square cardboard piece owned by its faction or hireling.

title: Cannot
text: See 1.1.2. The term cannot is absolute. It cannot be overridden unless explicitly instructed.

title: Discard
text: Place the prompted card in the shared discard pile. If it is a dominance card, place it near the map instead (3.3.3). Lizard Frog

title: Draw
text: Take a card into your hand. If drawing from a deck or pile, take the top card unless otherwise specified. If no source is specified, take it from the shared deck (2.1). Frog

title: Effect
text: Anything that changes the game, including persistent effects, faction abilities, and actions.

title: Enemy
text: Any other player that you are not in a coalition with (9.2.8), or a hireling that is in the supply or held by an enemy player.

title: Enemy Piece
text: A faction piece of an enemy player or a hireling piece of an enemy hireling, except while you're treating the piece as your own for rule (Riverfolk mercenaries, controlled hirelings, etc.). (Items cannot be enemy pieces.)

title: Faction Piece
text: All the warriors, pawns, buildings, and tokens listed on the back of a faction board. (Items are not faction pieces.) See 1.5.1.

title: Forest
text: An area on the map enclosed by paths and clearings.

title: Item
text: A square cardboard piece showing an item (Boot, Sword, Crossbow, etc.) that is not owned by any faction.

title: Map
text: See 2.2.

title: Map Edge
text: The single closed loop of clearings and paths that define the map boundary, including closed paths on the mountain map.

title: Matching
text: Of the same suit.

title: Path
text: A white link between two clearings.

title: Pawn
text: A wooden figure owned by its faction or hireling.

title: Piece
text: Any component—building, token, warrior, pawn, item, marker, and so on.

title: Place
text: Take the prompted piece from the prompted source and put it in the prompted destination. Usually, no source is specified—in this case, take it from its supply, or take the leftmost prompted piece if it is on a track. Put is shorthand for Place.

title: Play Area
text: The area around your faction board. Cards in it can only be spent, discarded, or used for other purposes if explicitly instructed.

title: Random
text: When referring to a card, choose one at random without looking at them at all.

title: Replace
text: Remove the prompted piece and place the other prompted piece in the location from which the first was removed. To do so, you must be able to complete both steps. (For example, enemies of the Marquise cannot replace a Marquise warrior at the keep.)

title: Remove
text: Take the prompted piece from the prompted source and return it to the prompted destination. Usually, no destination is specified—in this case, return it to its owner's supply, return it to the rightmost empty space of its track it has one, or remove it permanently otherwise. (Items are removed permanently.)

title: Reveal
text: Place the prompted card face up in your play area. Usually, no source is specified—in this case, take it from your hand.

title: River
text: A blue link between two clearings.

title: Ruin
text: Piece covering an "R" slot in a clearing (2.2.4).

title: Rule
text: A player rules a clearing if they have more total warriors and buildings in it than each other player. (Tokens and pawns do not contribute to rule.) If there is a tie between players in a clearing, no one rules it.

title: Show
text: Let the prompted player see the prompted piece.

title: Slot
text: White box in a clearing 2.2.3.

title: Spend
text: See Discard. (These terms are equivalent, but spend is used in contexts with choice.)

title: Supply
text: The collection of pieces that is not on a faction board or the map. The item supply is the collection of items on the map.

title: Swap
text: Switch the locations of the two prompted pieces. (This ignores MOVE and PLACE restrictions, such as the Corvids' snare and the Marquise's keep.)

title: Token
text: A circular cardboard piece owned by its faction or hireling.

title: Treat
text: The prompted thing takes on the properties of the second prompted thing. While you treat enemy pieces as your own for rule, they are not enemy pieces, but they are still faction pieces of that enemy player. (For example, Riverfolk warriors you've hired as mercenaries are not enemy pieces to you, but they are still Riverfolk faction pieces.)

title: Warrior
text: A wooden figure owned by its faction or hireling. (The Vagabond pawn is not a warrior and cannot be removed.)

title: Gaining from Supply
text: When a player's score marker enters a space with a hireling marker, they take the hireling marker and place it below their Evening (as a reminder). At the end of their turn, they take any hireling card from the supply, roll for control, and flip over the hireling marker.

title: Rolling for Control
text: When a player gains a hireling card, they roll the control die and place control markers on the hireling card equal in number to the die roll. They count only the gold die pips if they have the most victory points or are tied for the most; they count all the die pips otherwise (including if they have activated a dominance card).

title: Gaining from Another Player
text: At the end of a player's turn, they must remove one control marker from each hireling card they gained on previous turns. Then, they must give each hireling card they control that has no control markers, along with a hireling marker, to any other player (even the player with the highest score). That player puts the hireling marker below their Evening (as a reminder) and immediately rolls for control.

title: Abilities And Actions
text: Hirelings have various actions and abilities, as shown by unique icons. Actions and abilities that start with "controller:" are gained by the hireling's controller.

title: When-Hired Action ()
text: {hired}}). When they take control of the hireling, the controlling player must take this action.

title: Ability ()
text: {ability}}). This ability is always active or it specifies when it happens.

title: Start-of-Birdsong Action ()
text: {birdsong}}). At the start of their Birdsong, the controlling player must or may take this action, as the action describes.

title: Once-Per-Daylight Action ()
text: {daylight}}). Once in their Daylight, the controlling player may take this action.

title: Rule
text: A hireling's controller treats hireling pieces as their own only for rule. (The controller can rule a clearing even with hirelings alone.) Uncontrolled hirelings can rule clearings as if they were players.

title: Enemy Status
text: A hireling is an enemy to players other than its controller and players in coalition with its controller.

title: Separate Pieces
text: Hireling pieces are not the controller's faction pieces. (So, the Duchy cannot count them as Duchy pieces to sway, the Keepers cannot remove them to encamp, etc.)

title: Separate Actions
text: A hireling's Move or Battle actions can only move or battle with the hireling's pieces and cannot include the controller's pieces. Hirelings cannot take actions in other ways (such as from their controller's Move actions, False Orders, or the Vagabond's Allied Relationship).

title: Separate Effects
text: Hirelings cannot use their controller's abilities, crafted persistent effects, or ambush cards. (So, a hireling could not use Boat Builders while moving, and the Highway Bandits could not be placed on a river. A hireling's controller could not play an ambush card while battling with the hireling.)

title: No Scoring from Removal
text: A hireling's controller does not score victory points if their hireling removes an enemy piece (usually in battle). (Players can still score points by removing hireling buildings and tokens, even when defending in battle against the hireling. Players still score as normal if the Warm Sun Prophets force that player's faction pieces to battle.)

title: Weird Stuff
text: If you move hireling warriors into a clearing with an Alliance sympathy token or remove Alliance sympathy by using a hireling, this does trigger Outrage. (These effects refer to a "player moving" or "player removing.")

title: Safety
text: Landmarks cannot be battled, moved, covered, or removed, unless noted explicitly by a landmark.

title: Ownership
text: Landmarks are not owned by anyone and are not enemy pieces.

title: Autumn Map
text: No special rules.

title: Raging River
text: The river divides forests (as printed paths do).

title: Setup Modifications
text: Place the Ferry piece in the corner clearing that is also a coastal clearing.

title: The Lake
text: The lake is in the center of the map. The lake is treated as rivers linking each coastal clearing to each other coastal clearing. The lake divides forests.

title: Coastal Clearings
text: Clearings touching the lake (not separated by a forest) are coastal clearings.

title: Coastal Forests
text: Forests touching the lake are coastal forests. Each coastal forest is adjacent to its two neighboring coastal forests (separated by one coastal clearing).

title: The Ferry
text: Once per turn, when moving from a clearing with the Ferry, you may move to another coastal clearing, ignoring paths. Move the Ferry along with the moving pieces. If faction pieces move, their player draws one card. (You still must rule the origin or destination clearing to use the Ferry, even with the Swimmers ability. If pieces of multiple factions move at the same time, each of their players draws a card.)

title: Setup Modifications
text: Place the 6 closed path markers to cover the 6 paths of darker color with excavated ground. Place the Tower piece in the central clearing showing two towers.

title: Closed Paths
text: A path covered with a closed path marker is a closed path. Clearings linked by a closed path are not adjacent, and pieces (such as Highway Bandits) cannot be placed on closed paths. Closed paths enclose and divide forests as if they were paths (so the Vagabond can slip across it).

title: Removing Closed Paths
text: Once per turn in their Daylight, a player can spend a card to remove a closed path marker from the game permanently and score one victory point. To remove it, that player must have any faction pieces in either clearing linked by the closed path marker.

title: The Pass and Tower
text: The clearing marked with the Tower piece is the pass. At the end of a player's Evening, if that player rules the Pass, that player scores one victory point.

title: Forests
text: All areas on the mountain map enclosed by paths and clearings are forests, regardless of the presence or placement of trees within.

title: Setup Modification
text: Follow the subsection based on your player count. Then, place 2 ruins in the "R" slots with no numbers and 2 ruins in the "R" slots with the lowest showing numbers.

title: 1–4 Players
text: Cover a total of 3 flooding clearings with flood markers—one light green, one dark green, and one brown. Align the flood markers' paths so that they match up with paths touching the marker.

title: 5+ Players
text: Place the Mousehold, Foxburrow, and Rabbittown landmarks in the three unsuited clearings. (You can still place other landmarks as normal.)

title: Flooded Clearings
text: A flooded clearing is no longer a clearing. Instead it only contains one or more paths, and may include flooded paths. Clearings linked by any number of non-flooded paths in these clearings are adjacent.

title: Flooded Paths
text: Flooded paths are not linked to the other paths, but they enclose and divide forests as if they were paths (so the Vagabond can slip across it).

title: Placing on Paths
text: Pieces that can be placed on paths (such as Highway Bandits) can be placed on any non-flooded path in the clearing, but not the point where its paths link.

title: The Dam
text: The dam separates the forests under it.

title: The Bridge
text: The bridge is a path. The bridge does not separate the forests under it.

title: Gorge Sides
text: The gorge sides do not separate the forests they are in.

title: Special Action: Day Labor
text: Exhaust one Torch to take a card from the discard pile whose suit matches your clearing. (You can always take a bird card.)

title: Special Action: Hideout

title: Special Action: Instigate

title: Special Action: Protector
text: When defending in battle, before the roll, a faction may enlist the Arbiter if he's in the clearing of battle. If so, the Arbiter scores one victory point and adds all of his undamaged Sword to the defender's maximum rolled hits. The Arbiter cannot enlist himself or be enlisted against himself.

text: Start with Boot, Boot, Torch, Crossbow.

title: Special Action: Scorched Earth
text: Exhaust a Torch and place it in your clearing to remove all enemy pieces there. Pieces cannot be placed in or moved into the clearing with the Torch. (You remain in this clearing. Once you move out, you cannot move back in. The Torch cannot be removed with a "Favor of the..." card because it is not an enemy piece.)

title: Starting Items
text: Start with Boot, Torch, Hammer.

title: Special Action: Improvise
text: Once per turn while taking the Quest action, you may treat one unexhausted item as any other item. When you exhaust it to complete the quest, also damage that item.

title: Starting Items
text: Start with Coin, Torch, Sword, Crossbow.

title: Special Action: Glide
text: Exhaust a Torch to move only your Vagabond pawn (not other pieces) to any clearing (even Hostile) on the map, ignoring adjacency and paths, without exhausting any Boot.

title: Starting Items
text: Start with Boot, Boot, Torch, Sword.

title: Special Action: Swift Strike
text: You may exhaust a Sword to deal an extra hit in battle (after rolling).

title: Starting Items
text: Start with Boot, Tea, Crossbow, Torch.

title: Special Action: Con
text: Once per turn, you may resolve the Quest action by exhausting any two items instead of the listed items. (Score or draw as normal, and draw a new quest.) Then, shuffle the completed quest into the quest deck.

title: Starting Items
text: Start with Boot, Torch, Hammer.

title: Special Action: Duel
text: You may exhaust any item, damage it, and remove 1 enemy warrior from the Gladiator's clearing to draw 1 card. Do not go Hostile.

title: Starting Items
text: Start with Boot, Crossbow, Torch.

title: Special Action: Coerce
text: Once per turn, you may spend a card matching the Jailor's clearing to treat it as exhausting any item. After the action that it prompts or adds to, you lose 1 victory point. This action may interrupt actions on your turn. (You may use it to repair, craft, aid, quest, and pay for Riverfolk Services.)

title: Cost
text: Bots craft items without activating crafting pieces. (The items must still be in the supply to craft.)

title: Items
text: Whenever a bot crafts an item, it ignores the listed victory points and instead scores only one victory point.

title: Persistent Effects
text: Bots cannot craft cards with persistent effects.

title: Taking Hits
text: When taking hits, a bot removes all its tokens from the clearing of battle before removing any of its buildings there. If it has multiple types of buildings that it could remove there, it chooses to remove at random.

title: Dominance Cards
text: Bots cannot play a dominance card to change their victory condition.

title: Clearing Target Priority
text: If a bot must choose among clearings to target with an action, it follows all of the rules listed by its action. If it cannot target a clearing based on those rules, it targets the clearing of highest priority, as shown by the priority markers place on the map, from among the clearings it would have targeted based on those rules. The clearing of highest priority is marked "1", and the clearing of lowest priority is marked "12."

title: Player Target Priority
text: If a bot must choose among players to target with an action, it follows all rules all rules listed by its action. If it cannot target a player based on those rules it targets the player with the highest setup priority, starting with the Marquise de Cat with "A."

title: Target Legality
text: A bot can only target a prompted clearing or player if the rules allow it. If a bot cannot target a prompted clearing or player, it will attempt to target another clearing or player tied in target priority; if it has attempted to target all such clearings or players, it will attempt to target the clearing or player next in the order of target priority. (For example, if a bot is prompted to battle in the clearing with the most enemy warriors, but it has no warriors in that clearing, it will attempt to battle in another clearing with the most enemy warriors. If it has attempted to battle in every such clearing, it will attempt to battle in the clearing with the second most enemy warriors. This continues until it battles or it has attempted to battle in every clearing.)

title: Action Order
text: If a bot would take multiple actions with different targets that might produce different results based on the order of those actions, the bot takes them in order of highest to lowest target priority. When moving, asses the priority order of the origin clearings (not the destinations).

title: "Such A..."
text: The rules often use the term such a clearing. This term means "the clearing that follows all the criteria for targeting a clearing previously listed by this action." The rules also us the terms such clearings, such a player, and such players to similar effect.

title: "Humans" And "Bots"
text: The term player includes both human players and bot players, which are respectively referred to as humans and bots.

title: Order Cards
text: On its turn, a bot draws and reveals a card, called the order card, to determine some actions it takes. The term ordered means "matching the suit of the current order card."

title: Abilities
text: Every bot has the following two abilities.

title: Poor Manual Dexterity
text: The bots have no hand of cards. Bots cannot discard cards. If a human would take a card from a bot, that human draws a card instead. If a human would give a card to a bot, discard that card, and that bot scores one victory point.

title: Hates Surprises
text: Ambush cards cannot be played against bots. (The Automated Alliance does not list this ability because they never initiate battles.)

title: Place Priority Markers
text: After choosing the map, place a priority marker in each clearing as shown in the matching chart.

title: "5.1.1 Step 1: Assign Factions And Starting Player"
text: During this step of standard setup, you may replace any number of factions with the matching bot factions.

title: Choose Difficulty And Traits
text: After step 1 and before step 2 of standard setup, choose a difficulty and traits for each bot, as follows.

title: Difficulty
text: Choose a difficulty of easy, default, challenging, or nightmare. If you choose a difficulty other than default, place the matching difficulty card face up near the bot's faction board.

title: Traits
text: Each bot has four trait cards, which modify its rules and generally increase its difficulty. Choose any number of trait cards (even zero) and place them face up near the bot's faction board.

title: "5.1.3 Step 3: Draw Starting Hands"
text: Modify this step of standard setup as follows: "If you are playing with one or two humans, remove all four dominance cards from the deck. (Do not include the spy cards from the Riverfolk Expansion.) Shuffle the deck. Each human draws three cards. (Bots do not draw cards.)"

title: Fully Cooperative Play
text: If you want to play against the bots as a team, remove all four dominance cards during setup, and use the following rules in play.

title: Victory
text: To win, the humans must each score 30 victory points before any bot scores 30 victory points. Bots do not treat bot pieces as enemy pieces when targeting a clearing to act in, and do not target each other in battle. (However, a bot might still remove bot pieces as collateral damage with effects such as revolts, etc.) The humans still treat each other as enemies (so they can remove buildings and tokens for points, etc.).

title: Cooperative Variants
text: If you need a leg up on the bots and feel adventurous, you might try treating all the humans' pieces as on the same "team" in various ways, such as combining them when determining who rules clearings. When doing this, you'll need to make judgement calls about certain interactions (e.g., can the Lizard Cult convert a friendly Eyrie warrior using a conspiracy?). There are many such interactions in Root, and we'd encourage you to err on the side of challenge.

title: Overview
text: This is the simplest of the bots and can be used to fill out the player count in dozens of configurations. Though this bot is straightforward, don't get complacent. At least one player will need to keep it in check!

title: The Keep
text: Only the Marquise can place pieces in the clearing with the keep token. (Pieces may be moved into this clearing.) If the keep token is removed, remove it from the game permanently.

title: Step 1: Gather Warriors
text: Form a supply of 25 warriors near you.

title: Step 2: Place Keep
text: Place the keep token in a random corner clearing.

title: Step 3: Garrison
text: Place a warrior in each clearing except the clearing in the diagonally opposite corner from the clearing with the keep token. Place an extra warrior in the clearing with the keep token.

title: Step 4: Place Starting Buildings
text: Randomly place 1 sawmill, 1 workshop, and 1 recruiter among the clearing with the keep token and those clearings adjacent with up to one building in each clearing.

title: Step 5: Fill Buildings Tracks
text: Place your remaining 5 sawmills, 5 workshops, and 5 recruiters on your matching Buildings tracks, filling every space except the leftmost space of each track.

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has two steps in the following order.

title: Reveal Order
text: Draw and reveal an order card.

title: Craft Item
text: If the order card shows an available item, craft it.

title: Daylight
text: Your Daylight has five steps in the following order. If the order card is a bird card, resolve Escalated Daylight instead of this section.

title: Battle
text: Initiate a battle in each ordered clearing. The defender is the player with the most pieces in the clearing of battle.

title: First Tie for Defender
text: Such a player with the most victory points.

title: Recruit
text: Place four warriors among ordered clearings you rule, distributed evenly. If you rule three such clearings, place the fourth warrior in such a clearing of highest priority.

title: Build
text: Place a building in the clearing you rule with the most Marquise warriors. Place a sawmill if the order card is a fox card, a workshop if it is a rabbit card, or a recruiter if it is a mouse card. (The order card determines the type of building placed, not the clearing where it is placed.)

title: Move
text: Move all but three of your warriors from each ordered clearing to the adjacent clearing with the most enemy pieces.

title: Expand
text: If you did not place a building this turn and have five or fewer buildings on the map, discard the current order card, draw and reveal a new order card (but do not craft its item), and return to the start of Daylight.

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has two steps in the following order.

title: Score
text: Score victory points listed on the rightmost empty space on your ordered Buildings track. If the order card is a bird card, use the track that would score the most victory points. (Unlike the Marquise de Cat, you do not score victory points for placing buildings.)

title: Discard Order
text: Discard the current order card.

title: Escalated Daylight
text: If the order card is a bird card, resolve the following steps instead of Daylight, and then continue to Evening.

title: Battle
text: Initiate a battle in each clearing. The defender is the player with the most pieces in the clearing of battle.

title: First Tie for Defender
text: Such a player with the most victory points.

title: Recruit
text: Place two warriors each in the two clearings you rule of lowest priority. If you only rule one clearing, place all four warriors there.

title: Build
text: Place a building of the type with the most pieces on the map in the clearing you rule with the most Marquise warriors. If there is a tie between sawmills and any other types, place a sawmill. If there is a tie between workshops and recruiters but not sawmills, place a recruiter.

title: Move
text: Move all but three of your warriors from each clearing to the adjacent clearings with the most enemy pieces. Then battle in each clearing you moved into.

title: Overview
text: The Electric Eyrie will inspire fear in the most stalwart of players. Like the Eyrie Dynasties, this bot can ramp up its action potential aggressively.

title: Lords of the Forest
text: The Electric Eyrie rule a clearing when tied for most combined warriors and buildings there. They do not rule empty clearings.

title: Step 1: Gather Warriors
text: Form a supply of 20 warriors near you.

title: Step 2: Place Roost and Starting Warriors
text: Place 1 roost and 6 warriors in a random corner clearing that is not the starting corner clearing of another bot and, if possible, is diagonally opposite from a starting corner clearing.

title: Step 3: Tuck Viziers
text: Tuck your 2 Loyal Vizier cards, showing their suit, into the rightmost Decree column.

title: Step 4: Fill Roosts Track
text: Place your 6 remaining roosts on your Roosts track from right to left, filling all its spaces except the leftmost.

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has four steps in the following order.

title: Reveal Order
text: Draw and reveal an order card.

title: Craft Order
text: If the order card shows an available item, craft it.

title: Add to Decree
text: Add the order card to the Decree in the column matching the card's suit.

title: New Roost
text: st. If you have no roosts on the map, place a roost and four warriors in the ordered clearing of highest priority where all those pieces can be placed. (Intentionally not listed on board.)

title: Daylight
text: Your Daylight has two steps in the following order.

title: Resolve the Decree
text: Recruit for each column in the Decree with at least one card from left to right. Then move in the same way. Then battle in the same way.

title: Recruit
text: Place warriors, equal to the number of cards in this column, in a clearing with a roost whose suit matches this column's suit.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing with the most enemy pieces.

title: Second Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing with the fewest Eyrie warriors.

title: Third Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing of lowest priority.

title: Move
text: Move from the clearing you rule whose suit matches this column's suit and has the most Eyrie warriors. Move to an adjacent clearing with no roost–if all adjacent clearings have a roost, following the tiebreakers below. Leave warriors in the origin clearing so there are exactly enough to rule it or equal to the number of cards in this column, whichever is higher.

title: First Tie for Destination Clearing
text: Such a clearing with the fewest enemy pieces.

title: Second Tie for Destination Clearing
text: Such a clearing of lowest priority.

title: Battle
text: Initiate a battle in a clearing whose suit matches this column's suit. The defender is the player with the most buildings there (even zero). If this column has more cards than each other column, you deal one extra hit.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing with no roost.

title: Second Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing with the most defenseless buildings.

title: Third Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing of lowest priority.

title: First Tie for Defender
text: Such a player with the most pieces there.

title: Second Tie for Defender
text: Such a player with the most victory points.

title: Build
text: Place a roost in a clearing you rule with no roost. (If multiple, pick the clearing of highest priority.) If you cannot place a roost for any reason, you immediately fall into turmoil. (You will take this action regardless of which cards are in your Decree.)

title: Evening
text: Score the victory points listed on the rightmost empty space of your Roosts track.

title: Turmoil
text: If you are prompted to place a roost but cannot for any reason, you fall into turmoil, as follows.

title: Step 1: Humiliate
text: Lose one victory point per bird card (including Loyal Viziers) on the Decree.

title: Step 2: Purge
text: Discard all of the cards on the Decree except you Loyal Viziers. Keep you Loyal Viziers in the bird column.

title: Step 3: Rest
text: Go to Evening (as normal).

title: Overview
text: The Automated Alliance is especially zealous and will revolt frequently. Keep in mind their potential targets so you avoid any unpleasant surprises. Once they do establish a foothold, timing is critical. Don’t let them consolidate their warrior or you’ll be in trouble!

title: Sympathy Tokens
text: The Alliance has 10 sympathy tokens.

title: Placement Limits
text: A clearing can hold only one sympathy token.

title: Terms
text: A sympathetic clearing is one with a sympathy token. An unsympathetic clearing is one without a sympathy token.

title: Automated Ambush
text: In battle as defender with at least one Alliance warrior, the Alliance steals, one extra hit.

title: Automated Outrage
text: Whenever a human removes a sympathy token or moves any warriors into a sympathetic clearing, that player must discard a matching card. If they cannot, the Alliance scores one victory point. (this does not trigger poor manual dexterity.)

title: Crackdown
text: Whenever an Alliance base is removed, remove all sympathy tokens from clearings matching the suit of the base removed.

title: Martial Law
text: If the Alliance places a sympathy token in a clearing with three or more warriors owned by the same enemy, the Alliance scores one fewer victory point, to a minimum of zero.

title: Step 1: Gather Warriors
text: Form a supply of 10 warriors near you.

title: Step 2: Place Bases
text: Place your 3 bases on the matching spaces in your Bases box.

title: Step 3: Fill Sympathy Track
text: Place your 10 sympathy tokens on your Sympathy track.

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has four steps in the following order.

title: Reveal Order
text: Draw and reveal an order card.

title: Craft Order
text: If the order card shows an available item, craft it.

title: Revolt
text: If the order card is not a bird card, remove all enemy pieces from the ordered sympathetic clearing with the most enemy pieces matching a base on your faction board, then place the ordered base there.

title: Public Pity
text: If you did not revolt this turn in Birdsong, spread sympathy based on the number of sympathy tokens on the map, as follows. If you have zero to four, spread sympathy twice; if you have five or more, spread sympathy once. (You will spread sympathy again in Daylight.)

title: Daylight
text: Your Daylight has two steps in the following order.

title: Spread Sympathy
text: Place a sympathy token in an ordered unsympathetic clearing with the fewest enemy warriors adjacent to a sympathetic clearing. Score the victory points listed on the space revealed on your faction board (remembering Martial Law).

title: No Such Clearings
text: if there are no such clearings to target, place a sympathy token in the clearing with the fewest enemy pieces.

title: Cannot Spread
text: if you cannot place a sympathy token (because your Sympathy track is empty, or because there is no clearing where you could place a sympathy token), score 5 victory points.

title: Surprise Revolt
text: If the order card is a bird card, remove all enemy pieces from the sympathetic clearing with the most enemy pieces matching a base on your board, then place the matching base there. (If multiple, revolt in the clearing of highest priority.)

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has three steps in the following order.

title: Organize
text: In each clearing with a base and three or more Alliance warriors, remove all Alliance warriors from that clearing, and then spread sympathy.

title: Recruit
text: Place one warrior in each clearing with a base.

title: Discard Order
text: Discard the current order card.

title: Overview
text: The Vagabot makes for a capricious friend or foe. Like a human player, he will reward those who craft items. But be careful, he can make for a dangerous enemy once he gets enough items to boost his maximum hits.

title: Lone Wanderer
text: The Vagabot pawn is not a warrior (so he cannot rule a clearing or stop another player from ruling one). The Vagabot pawn cannot be removed from the map.

title: Full Removal
text: Whenever an enemy player uses an effect that says it removes all enemy pieces from a clearing (such as Alliance revolts, Favor of the Mice cards, Conspiracy bombs) with the Vagabot, he damages three items.

title: Nimble
text: The Vagabot can move regardless of who rules his origin or destination clearing.

title: Items
text: To take actions, the Vagabot must exhaust items. Unlike the Vagabond, the Vagabot treats all items as identical (for example, there is no difference between  and ). Items on the Vagabot's faction board can be face up or face down. He exhausts undamaged items, flipping them face down, to take many actions. When gained, all items are placed face up in his Satchel.

title: Battle Track
text: The Vagabot's maximum rolled hits in battle begins at one. (The Vagabot does not count  toward this.) While the Vagabot has at least six, nine, and twelve undamaged items, one, two, or three items, exhausted before unexhausted, are placed on the spaces of the Vagabot's Battle Track from left to right. The sixth and ninth items each increase his maximum rolled hits by one, and the twelfth item makes him deal one extra hit as attacker in battle. Items on the Battle Track cannot be exhausted, but they can be damaged.

title: Taking Hits
text: When the Vagabot takes hits, he damages exhausted items or, if he has no exhausted items, unexhausted items. (Damaging items may move items from its Battle Track to its Satchel.)

title: Step 1: Choose Character
text: Pick a character card and place it in your Character Card slot. (These are different from the character cards for the Vagabond.)

title: Step 2: Place Pawn
text: Place you Vagabot pawn in the forest adjacent to the most clearings. If there are multiple such forests, decide randomly among those.

title: Step 3: Get Quests
text: Shuffle the quest deck, draw 1 quest card, and place it face up near you. This quest can only be completed by the bot.

title: Step 4: Populate Ruins
text: Take the 4 items marked "R" and place one randomly under each ruin. (This is the same as the human Vagabond.)

title: Step 5: Take Starting Items
text: Take any 4 items marked "S" and place them in your Satchel. (The Tinker starts with 3 items instead of 4 items.)

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has three steps in the following order.

title: Reveal Order
text: Draw and reveal an order card.

title: Craft Order
text: If the order card shows an available item, craft it.

title: Slip
text: If you have two or fewer undamaged items, move into a random adjacent forest, then skip Daylight and begin Evening.

title: Daylight
text: The current order card determines the sequence of actions that you will take this turn, as follows. Often, you will be prompted to take an action in the nearest clearing. If you can take the action without moving, remain in your current clearing. If you cannot, move to a clearing where you can take the action, exhausting one item per move in the way that exhausts the fewest items. You move even if you do not have enough unexhausted items to take the action after moving.

title: Explore
text: Move to the nearest ruin. Then, exhaust one item to take one random item under the ruin in your clearing, reveal it, and place it face up in your Satchel. If you remove the last item from the ruin, remove the ruin. (Do not score victory points for exploring.)

title: Quest
text: Moved to the nearest clearing, matching the current quest. Then, exhaust two items to complete the quest. (Ignore the listed item types on the card.) Discard the quest and score one victory point. (Ignore the text affect of the card.) Then, draw a new quest and place it face up near you.

title: Aid
text: Target, the player in the clearing with at least one piece there, at least one item in their crafted item box, and the fewest victory points of such players there. Exhaust as many items as possible up to the number of items in their crafted items box. Take that many items from the target player and score that many victory points, then the target player draws that many cards. (You can aid other bots. Because of their Poor Manual Dexterity, aided bots simply score one victory point.)

title: Battle
text: Move to the nearest clearing with at least one piece of the player with the most victory points. Then, exhaust one item to initiate a battle against that player. If any pieces of that player remain, exhaust two items and battle again, repeating this until you do not have enough items to exhaust. Score one victory point per enemy warrior you remove. (Do not score this if you are the defender. You still score points for removing tokens and buildings.)

title: First Tie for Destination Clearing
text: Such a clearing where the target defender has the most buildings and tokens.

title: Second Tie for Destination Clearing
text: Such a clearing where the target defender has the fewest warriors.

title: Repair
text: If you have at least one damaged item, exhaust one item to repair it. All unexhausted, damaged items must be repaired before any exhausted, damaged items can be repaired. (Do not flip the repaired item face up if it is faced down.)

title: Special
text: Exhaust one item to take the action listed on your character card. If the special action listed on your character card would have no effect or is impossible, skip this action.

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has three steps in the following order.

title: Refresh
text: If you have at least one damaged item, refresh for undamaged items. If you have no damaged items, refresh six undamaged items instead.

title: Repair
text: If you’re in a forest, repair all items. If you are not in a forest, repair one item. Repair unexhausted items before exhausted items.

title: Thief (Easy)
text: Take a random card from the enemy in your clearing with the most victory points. On a tie, take it from such an enemy with the most pieces there.

title: Tinker (Moderate)
text: Search the discard pile for the topmost card with an available item and crafted. (Remember to only score one point.) You start with one fewer item.

title: Ranger (Difficult)
text: If you have three or more damaged items, slip into a random adjacent forest.

title: Vagrant
text: Initiate a battle in your clearing. You choose both attacker and defender, and you remove pieces for each.

title: Scoundrel
text: If you’re clearing has three or more enemy pieces, including one building or token, remove all enemy pieces, there. Place one of your items in your clearing, covering a building slot. Buildings cannot be placed in this slot. Score one point.

title: Arbiter
text: Before rolling in battle, the defender may enlist the Arbiter if he is in the battle clearing. (If other bots are in place, they will interact with the Arbiter, whether played by a human or bot, in the same way.) The Arbiter scores one victory point and adds the number of items on his bow track to the defenders. Maximum rolled hits. Defending bots will enlist the Arbiter if they meet all three of the following conditions:

title: One
text: Their maximum rolled hits is less than three.

title: Two
text: Their maximum rolled hits is less than the number of enemy pieces in battle.

title: Three
text: They have more victory points than the Arbiter.

title: Overview
text: The Lizards will convert all unbelievers to their cause, whether they're willing or not. Keep an eye on their Lost Souls, and prepare for a flood of warriors if you see lots of cards matching the clearings you're in. Try to hurt them whenever possible by removing their gardens, and watch out if you give them too many acolytes.

title: Pilgrims
text: You rule clearings that have a garden. (As normal)

title: Robot Revenge
text: Whenever any number of Lizard warriors are removed, place one of them in the Lizards' Acolytes box instead of their supply.

title: Gardens
text: When a garden is removed from the map, discard the top card in the Lizards' Lost Souls pile face up.

title: Lost Souls
text: Whenever a card is spent or discarded, place it on the top of the Lizards' Lost Souls pile face up.

title: Step 1: Gather Warriors
text: Form a supply of 25 warriors.

title: Step 2: Place Warriors
text: Place 4 warriors and 1 garden of matching printed suit in a random corner clearing that is not the starting corner clearing of another bot and, if possible, is diagonally opposite from a starting corner clearing. Then place 1 warrior in each adjacent clearing.

title: Step 3: Set Conspiracy
text: Place the outcast marker on the Sanctify space of the Conspiracy track on your faction board.

title: Step 4: Fill Gardens Tracks
text: Place your 14 remaining gardens on the matching spaces of your Gardens tracks from right to left.

title: Step 5: Draw Lost Souls
text: Draw 3 cards and place them face up in your Lost Souls in the order drawn.

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has two steps in the following order.

title: Set Order
text: The order is the most common suit in your Lost Souls. On a tie, the order is bird.

title: Perform Conspiracies
text: If you have any acolytes, move the Conspiracy marker one space to the right; if you move it off the right end, move it to the leftmost space. Then, perform the conspiracy of the covered space if able, and remove an acolyte if you do perform the conspiracy. Continue this process until you have no acolytes. Determine the target player first, then determine the target clearing.

title: Convert
text: In an ordered clearing, replace an enemy warrior with a Lizard warrior.

title: First Tie for Target Player
text: Player with the most points.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Clearing with the most enemy buildings.

title: Crusade
text: Battle in each ordered clearing with two or more Lizard warriors.

title: First Tie for Defender
text: Player in the battle clearing with the most points.

title: Sanctify
text: In an ordered clearing, replace an enemy building with a garden matching the clearing's printed suit.

title: First Tie for Target Player
text: Player with the most points.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Clearing with the fewest enemy warriors.

title: Daylight
text: Reveal the top four cards from your Lost Souls pile, one at a time. (They're already face up, so just put them in your play area.) For each, perform a ritual based on the suit of the card.

title: Rabbit, Fox, or Mouse Card
text: Place a warrior in a matching clearing. Then, if you rule that clearing, place a matching garden there.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Place the warrior in a clearing with free building slots, then most enemy buildings.

title: Bird Card
text: Remove one Lizard warrior from the clearing with the most Lizard warriors and place it in the Acolytes box instead of your supply. Put the revealed card in the discard pile (not the Lost Souls).

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has four steps in the following order.

title: Score
text: Score the points shown above the Gardens track for the rightmost empty, ordered Gardens space. (If your order is bird, score the track that has the fewest gardens.)

title: Discard Lost Souls
text: Discard all cards in your Lost Souls pile.

title: Return Revealed Cards
text: Return all your revealed cards to your Lost Souls, maintaining the order that you revealed them in. (The first card revaled goes on top.)

title: Craft
text: Reveal the top card of the deck and craft it, scoring one victory point, if it shows an available item. Then, add the revealed card to the top of your Lost Souls (even if you did not craft it).

title: Overview
text: If you need a shiny sword or a good boat, the Riverfolk can supply. The more services you buy from them, the stronger they become, but they'll turn nasty if no one buys anything from them. Watch out – these robots don't rust!

title: The Market
text: The Market is a row of five face-up cards. The order of its cards cannot be changed.

title: Trade Posts
text: Unlike for the Riverfolk human, trade posts that are removed from the map return to the Riverfolk bot's faction board.

title: Services
text: At the start of their Birdsong, another player may buy one service plus one service per clearing that has their faction pieces and a trade post. They pay for services by placing warriors in the Riverfolk's Payment box. If their faction owns no warriors, the Riverfolk place an equal number of Riverfolk warriors instead. A service's cost depends on the buyer's current victory points: two warriors if they have 0 to 9 points; three warriors if they have 10 to 19 points; four warriors if they have 20 or more points.

title: Hand Card
text: Take any card from the Market and add it to your hand. (As normal.)

title: Riverboats
text: Treat rivers as paths until the end of your turn. (As normal.)

title: Mercenaries
text: For battle and rule in Daylight and Evening, treat Riverfolk warriors as your own except for battle against the Riverfolk. In battle, you must split hits between your faction pieces and Riverfolk warriors. (As normal.)

title: Protectionism
text: Whenever you Organize, you will check whether you fulfill the shield and sword Protectionism conditions, as follows. If the Payments box is empty, you fulfill the shield condition. If you have no warriors in your supply, you fulfill the sword condition. If you fulfill the shield or sword condition, you will take every action that shows the matching icon for the rest of this turn.

title: Step 1: Gather Warriors
text: Form a supply of 15 warriors.

title: Step 2: Place Warriors
text: Place 1 warrior in each clearing on the river.

title: Step 3: Fill Trade Posts Tracks
text: Place 9 trade posts on the matching spaces of your Trade Posts tracks.

title: Step 4: Gain Starting Payment
text: Place 1 warrior in your Payments box.

title: Step 5: Stock Market
text: Draw 5 cards and add them to your Market.

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has three steps in the following order.

title: Stock the Market
text: Draw cards and add them face up to the Market's right side until it has five cards.

title: Craft
text: Craft the first card added to the Market this turn that shows an available item, scoring one victory point. (Discard it, leaving four cards.)

title: Set Order
text: The order is the rightmost Market card.

title: Daylight
text: Your Daylight has four steps in the following order.

title: Build and Garrison
text: Place a trade post and a warrior in an ordered clearing without a trade post.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing with any faction pieces of the player who has the most warriors in Payments.

title: Recruit
text: Place one warrior in each ordered clearing. If the order card is a bird card, instead place one warrior in each clearing on the river.

title: Warrior Limit
text: If you will run out of warriors when placing these warriors, place in highest priority clearing first.

title: Organize
text: Check whether you fulfill Protectionism conditions. Then, if the sword or shield Protectionism condition is fulfilled, score one victory point and place two warriors in a clearing that has Riverfolk pieces and the most enemy pieces.

title: Battle
text: If the shield Protectionism condition is fulfilled, battle in each clearing, and skip to Evening (ignoring the sword condition). Then, if the sword condition is fulfilled, battle in each ordered clearing.

title: First Tie for Defender
text: Battle the player with the fewest warriors in the Payments box.

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has three steps in the following order.

title: Score
text: Score one point for each warrior in the Payments box of the player who has the most warriors in your Payments box. Remove all of those warriors (returning them to their faction's supply).

title: Racketeering
text: If the sword or shield Protectionism condition is fulfilled, take all but two Riverfolk warriors from each clearing, and place them in the Payments box.

title: Discard
text: Discard the leftmost card in the Market. If the shield Protectionism condition is fulfilled, discard the leftmost card in the Market again.

title: Bot Services
text: The rules for bots interacting with the Riverfolk's services, whether the Riverfolk is a human or a bot, are listed on two sets of cards: 3 Basic Services and 8 Advanced Services. You can use only the Basic Services, or you can use both the Basic Services and the Advanced Services for any bots in play.

title: Overview
text: The Duchy has begun their invasion of the Woodland from the great lands below, emerging from fresh tunnels at a moment's notice. As they secure their foothold, their ministers will grow bold and add to the Duchy's capabilities. Punish them by destroying their buildings, driving them back into the dark.

title: Cost of Errors
text: Whenever any number of Duchy buildings are removed, remove the crown from the minister with a crown closest to the bottom.

title: The Burrow
text: The Burrow is an unsuited clearing adjacent to each clearing with a tunnel token. Non-Duchy pieces cannot b e placed in or moved into the Burrow. The Duchy always rules the Burrow (even with no pieces there). (As normal)

title: Step 1: Gather Pieces
text: Form supplies of 20 warriors, 3 tunnel tokens, and 9 crowns.

title: Step 2: Prepare the Burrow
text: Place the Burrow board near the map.

title: Step 3: Surface
text: Place 2 warriors and 1 tunnel in a corner clearing that is not the starting corner clearing. Then place 2 warriors in each clearing adjacent to the chosen corner clearing, except the Burrow.

title: Step 4: Fill Buildings Tracks
text: Place 3 citadels and 3 markets on your matching Building spaces.

title: Step 5: Sway Starting Ministers
text: Draw 2 cards and discard them. For each, place a crown on the topmost matching unswayed minister on your faction board.

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has three steps in the following order.

title: Set Order
text: Reveal the top card of the deck as the order card.

title: Craft
text: Craft the order card, scoring one victory point, if it shows an available item.

title: Recruit
text: Place two warriors, plus one per Mole icon showing on your faction board, into the Burrow.

title: Daylight
text: Your Daylight has four steps in the following order.

title: Dig
text: If the Burrow has four or more warriors, place a tunnel in an ordered clearing that has no tunnel and no Duchy buildings, then move four warriors from the Burrow to that clearing.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: If the order is not a bird, target such a clearing with the most empty building slots, then the fewest warriors. If the order card is a bird, target such a clearing with the most enemy buildings and tokens.

title: No Tunnel in Supply
text: If you have no tunnels in your supply to place, take a tunnel from the clearing with the fewest Duchy warriors in order to place it.

title: Battle
text: Battle in each ordered clearing.

title: First Tie for Defender
text: Battle the player with the most buildings there, then the most pieces there, then the most points there.

title: Build
text: In the clearing you rule with the most Duchy warriors, place a citadel if you have nine or more warriors in your supply, or otherwise place a market. If you cannot place a building and have any buildings on your faction board, score one victory point.

title: Act with Ministers
text: Take the actions of all swayed ministers, from top to bottom. (The Captain and Foremole have abilities. Do not take actions for them.)

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has four steps in the following order.

title: Rally
text: In each ordered clearing with no Duchy buildings and two or fewer Duchy warriors, move all Duchy warriors there to an adjacent clearing with a Duchy building. Then, in each clearing you rule, take all but four Duchy warriors from that clearing and place them in the Burrow.

title: First Tie for Destination
text: Such a clearing with the fewest Duchy warriors.

title: No Such Destination
text: If there is no adjacent clearing that has Duchy buildings, instead take all Duchy warriors there and place them in the Burrow.

title: Score
text: Score one victory point per market on the map.

title: Sway
text: Place a crown on the topmost ordered minister that has no crown. If no minister is ordered (including if the order is a bird), place a crown on the bottommost minister that has no crown.

title: Discard Order
text: Discard the order card.

title: Captain
text: As attacker in battle, deal an extra hit if the battle clearing has a tunnel. (This is an ability.)

title: Marshal
text: Place a warrior in the clearing that has fewest Duchy warriors and at least one Duchy building.

title: Foremole
text: In your Recruit step, place one more warrior in the Burrow. (This is an ability.)

title: Brigadier
text: If the Burrow has three or more warriors, take the Dig action. For this Dig action, its First Tie for Target Clearing is "such a clearing with the most enemy buildings or tokens."

title: Banker
text: Take the Build action.

title: Mayor
text: Remove a Duchy warrior from the clearing you rule that has the most Duchy warriors. If you do, score on victory point.

title: Earl of Stone
text: Score one victory point per citadel on the map.

title: Baron of Dirt
text: Score one victory point per market on the map.

title: Duchess of Mud
text: Score two victory points if all tunnels are on the map.

title: Overview
text: The Corvids want to rule by fear – and you will fear them unless you crush them with an iron fist. Snuff out their plots before they have a chance to resolve them, and watch out for large build-ups of warriors, as this will let them hatch plots and resolve them immediately.

title: Nimble
text: The Corvids can move regardless of who rules their origin or destination clearing. (As normal.)

title: Embedded Agents
text: As defender in battle, if the Corvids have a facedown plot token (even defenseless) in the clearing of battle, they deal an extra hit. (As normal.)

title: Step 1: Gather Warriors and Plots
text: Form supplies of 15 warriors and 8 plot tokens face down.

title: Step 2: Scatter
text: Place 1 warrior in the lowest priority clearing of each suit (total of 3).

title: Birdsong
text: Your Birdsong has four steps in the following order.

title: Set Order
text: Reveal the top card of the deck as the order card.

title: Craft
text: Craft the order card, scoring one victory point, if it shows an available item.

title: Recruit
text: Place two warriors in each of two ordered clearings.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Such a clearing with no plot tokens, then with most Corvid warriors.

title: No Warriors Left in Supply
text: If you have no warriors to place (even in the middle of this action), immediately do The Plot Thickens before placing the remaining warriors.

title: Flip Plots
text: Flip each facedown plot token. (A warrior is not needed to flip. Remember to resolve in priority order.) Each time you flip a plot, score one victory point for each face-up plot token on the map, then resolve the plot's flip effect, if any.

title: Daylight
text: Your Daylight has four steps in the following order.

title: Battle
text: Battle in each ordered clearing that has two or more Corvid warriors.

title: First Tie for Defender
text: Player with the most buildings and tokens there, then with the most victory points there.

title: Move
text: Move all but two Corvid warriors from each ordered clearing that has a face-up plot token to an adjacent clearing that has no plot token.

title: First Tie for Destination
text: Move to the clearing with the most Corvid warriors.

title: No Destination
text: If every adjacent clearing has a plot, move to the adjacent clearing of lowest priority.

title: Plot
text: In the ordered clearing that has the most Corvid warriors and no plot, remove one Corvid warrior there to place a random facedown plot there.

title: The Plot Thickens
text: If any clearing has no plot and three or more Corvid warriors, remove one Corvid warrior from it to place a random facedown plot token there.

title: First Tie for Target Clearing
text: Do this in the clearing with the most Corvid warriors.

title: Evening
text: Your Evening has two steps in the following order.

title: Score
text: Score one victory point per Extortion plot token face up on the map.

title: Discard Order
text: Discard the order card.

title: Bomb
text: When flipped, remove all enemy pieces in its clearing, then swap this token with a random plot token from your supply, placing the swapped plot face up. (The replacement token does not trigger, and it can be another bomb.)

title: Snare
text: While face up, enemy pieces cannot be placed in or moved from its clearing (as normal).

title: Extortion
text: When flipped, each player with any faction pieces in its clearing must discard one card.

title: Raid
text: When removed, place one warrior in each adjacent clearing (as normal).

title: Bot Interactions
text: The plots of the Corvids, whether played by a human or bot, interact with bots as follows.

title: Bomb
text: When flipped, remove two pieces of each bot in the clearing, warriors first, instead of all their pieces.

title: Snare
text: Bots ignore snare tokens for the purpose of targeting clearings to place or move pieces. If a bot would place in a clearing with a snare or move out of a clearing with a snare, remove the snare but do not perform this part of the action.

title: Ferry
text: The bots use the Ferry following normal movement rules, treating the Ferry as if the clearing with the Ferry and all other coastal clearings were linked by a path. (They score one victory point instead of drawing a card, as normal for bots.)

title: Closed Paths
text: The bots treat closed paths as paths, and they ignore rules for opening closed paths.

title: The Pass
text: When a bot attempts to target a clearing based on highest or lowest priority, the Pass will always meet this condition. (Bots will likely target the Pass, and it will win all tiebreakers.)
